| wl-0009 | Calculated columns and rows — derived tallies, recomputed on edit | A total typed into a table is a claim that goes stale the moment any row it summarises changes, and nothing detects it — precisely the class plan 001 spent four phases cataloguing: a figure that was true when written. dd already renders .dd.md deterministically from .dd.json, so a tally computed at build time CANNOT rot: it is derived, never asserted, and `dd build --check` already fails on drift. This turns a whole category of stale-number defect into an impossibility rather than a discipline. | idea | m | shape not settled — see the open questions in the note | Jordan 2026-08-08, verbatim: "next wishlist item is calculated columns (auto gens the total on edits, ato adds total column at bottom. cal tally cols and rows with setting." | AS ASKED: totals regenerate on edit (any set/add/rm touching a tallied section), a total row is appended automatically, and both column and row tallies are configurable by a setting. OPEN SHAPE QUESTIONS, recorded rather than guessed: (1) does the setting live in the SCHEMA — a field declares itself summable, so every document of that type tallies alike — or in the DOCUMENT, per-instance? Schema-side is more deterministic and matches how dd resolves everything else; document-side is more flexible. (2) Which aggregates: sum only, or count/min/max/mean? (3) Do tallies MATERIALISE into the .dd.json, or exist only in the rendered .dd.md? Render-only keeps the source a single truth and avoids write amplification on every edit, which argues strongly for it — and it is the option that makes the total underivable-from-anything-but-the-data. (4) What happens to a non-numeric or empty cell in a tallied column — skip, zero, or refuse? Refusing fits this repo: a silently-skipped cell produces a wrong total that looks right, which is the exact failure mode the feature exists to remove. |

SHAPE QUESTIONS for the design flow, recorded not guessed: (1) where do rules live — beside the schema (travelling with the family, so any repo resolving that schema inherits its rules) or in the consuming repo (local conventions over a shared family)? Both are wanted; the resolution order matters more than either. (2) How expressive: declarative predicates over the typed graph (cardinality, required-link-of-type, cross-document reachability) or an escape hatch to real code? A jiti-loaded custom type already exists as precedent for the escape hatch. (3) Are violations errors, warnings, or severity-declared by the rule? The plan validator already distinguishes ERROR from contradiction-class WARN, so severity is already a live concept. (4) NON-VACUITY: a rule engine can silently match nothing. Every rule needs to be provably capable of firing — the same requirement this repo puts on its own guards, and the reason plan 001 found a pin whose docstring claimed more than it pinned. |
